question: Should `policy watch --interval-ms` continue accepting equivalent decimal spellings such as `+500` and `0500`, or should Policy intentionally require one canonical textual representation?
rationale: The existing parser explicitly accepts these forms, they produce the same interval, and current documentation does not establish canonical spelling, so source inspection cannot determine whether breaking them is desired product policy.

options.title: Preserve accepted spellings
options.body: Keep the current parser because the reported inputs retain the requested numeric cadence and no documented contract requires canonical text.

options.title: Adopt canonical-only syntax
options.body: Approve the compatibility break, document the canonical decimal requirement, and require real CLI before/after/control proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Preserve accepted spellings
recommendation.body: Keep the current parser because the reported inputs retain the requested numeric cadence and no documented contract requires canonical text.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged Policy CLI and are the strongest available feature-history owner for this contract choice.
